judgment.notes: N001 and N007 apply to the same smooth real mean-zero datum and the grid defined in D011. On each step used, w=v(t_n) has norm below M and delta_n<=E_I<=1, so N008 and N009 apply with q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I<=2. N005 is used on intervals of length at most one with continuous piecewise smooth X inputs; its negative-norm slot may be any selected high input or Y_n. N006 applies to the mean-zero smooth inputs, and piecewise identities have cancelling interface endpoints. No E/M application occurs.

S001 sums at most h/tau+1 residual increments, including partial endpoints, and bounds e' by C_M E_I+C_M(tau^gamma+E_I) in H^(-pstar), giving the asserted X estimates. S002's differentiated terms combine as C(e,g,g)-C(e,g,e)/2=C(e,g,V), with g=v-e/2; the forcing signs and coefficients are correct and both boundary values contribute C_M N^(-1)E_I. In S003 the high-input decomposition yields h times the product of X norms plus N^(-pstar) times the product of L2 norms. Each cubic term contains e, giving C_M h tau^gamma+C_M(h+N^(-pstar))E_I. On a step portion of length ell<=tau, the forcing terms C(Y,z,V) and C(Y,Y,V) are bounded respectively by C_M(ell q_n+tau q_n) and C_M(ell q_n^2+tau q_n^2), hence by C_M tau q_n. The W term is bounded by (ell/tau)C_M||W||_2||V||_2<=C_M ell q_n. Summation gives the stated forcing bound. S004 combines these with the low-frequency bound and residual estimate to obtain precisely N010. No limiting exchange is needed; continuity and finite piecewise integration suffice.

Every substantive premise is a listed direct input or F001/F002 established earlier under L1. The exact flow is supplied by N001 and the numerical interpolation by D011/D027 and N007; no numerical Sobolev bound is assumed. Since a is a grid point, all steps with positive-length intersection start inside I, so their grid errors are bounded by E_I without using an error outside I. Local g, Fourier projections and integral are definitions; the threshold is arbitrary. S004 discharges L1 and retains its conditions in the output. The background notes justify only routine norm/integration and multiplier steps.

The full implication replays from the stated direct premises, supplied definitions, displayed local normal-form calculation and the positively checked routine background below. In particular the negative Y_n norm and W_n size needed for the forcing estimate are explicitly exported by N008; no absent producer argument is used. Packet permission fields add no mathematical premise. This judgment concerns mathematical sufficiency within the packet boundary.

D001–D004 fix the torus, Fourier normalization, Sobolev norms and Airy group; D016–D020 define the exponent, operators and X norm. D011 and D022–D030 specify the grid, stages, interpolation and residual, while N007 supplies the required gluing property. S002/S003 explicitly define the cutoff multipliers and auxiliary integral. The output retains the smooth datum restriction, grid-start condition, h<=1, 0<tau<=1, E_I<=1, every N>=2, all four estimates, partial final steps and the declared constant dependence.
